integration: Exact selectors and state sampler supplied; native viewer playback and geometry-anchored overlays deferred.

functional_sequences.mechanism: Arterial blood enters the open cord compartment before returning through sinus-wall slits to venous drainage.

steps.caption: Follow a representative arterial route from trabecula into white pulp.
steps.cue: Highlight arterial wall selectors sequentially; no membrane-crossing cue.

steps.caption: Penicillar arterioles continue into capillaries, some with cellular sheaths.
steps.cue: The sheath is surrounding tissue; the capillary lumen continues through it.

steps.caption: The capillary ends openly in the cords, separate from the venous sinus wall.
steps.cue: Stop the enclosed-path cue at the capillary end; use a separate diffuse cord-domain cue.

steps.caption: Blood contacts the cord compartment and its phagocytic cells.
steps.cue: Sparse schematic tokens within an extracellular tissue domain; no continuous connecting tube.

steps.caption: Red cells return from the cords through interendothelial slits into sinuses.
steps.cue: Direction is outside-to-inside across a lateral wall opening, never through an endothelial cell.

steps.caption: Sinuses collect into pulp veins and then trabecular veins.
steps.cue: Separate semantic drainage arrow; sampled sinuses are not asserted to join the authored pulp vein.

schematic_limitations: This field represents sampled vessels, not a complete perfusable graph.
The arterial-to-venous discontinuity is anatomical open circulation, not a construction defect.
2022 reconstruction supports wholly open human microcirculation in studied specimens; no percentage of open versus closed flow is assigned.
Display speed, marker frequency and schematic arrows do not estimate pressure, velocity or cell density.

functional_sequences.mechanism: Cell geometry and deformability determine mechanical passage; retained cells may subsequently be removed by macrophages.

steps.caption: Locate the cord side, longitudinal endothelial staves, wall slit and sinus lumen.
steps.cue: Local detail inset should name the normal transit axis and both in-plane slit axes.

steps.caption: A deformable red cell approaches from the cord side.
steps.cue: An enlarged RBC icon is an overlay, not a source cell or density measurement.

steps.caption: The cell deforms with a constricted waist as it crosses the short, narrow slit.
steps.cue: Use a labeled shape-state series: disc, leading lobe and waist, trailing lobe, recovered disc; do not isotropically shrink the cell.

steps.caption: A passing cell reaches the lumen and can recover its shape.
steps.cue: Complete crossing before recovery; conservation of cell surface and volume requires separate mechanical validation.

steps.caption: Altered geometry or low deformability can prevent successful passage.
steps.cue: Stop the second cell on the cord side; compare outcomes without asserting a diagnosis or threshold.

steps.caption: Mechanical retention and macrophage recognition are distinct processes.
steps.cue: Optional macrophage icon may engulf a retained cell in a separate later stage; no instant slit-induced lysis.

schematic_limitations: Shape states are conceptual; no finite-element membrane mechanics, fluid forces or cellular biophysics are solved.
Preserve authored slit short-axis 0.65 micrometres and transit depth 1.89 micrometres; source code uses 750 micrometres/model unit.
The slit long axis is authored as 2.5 micrometres; sinus calibre is separately magnified 1.4x.
Different RBC alterations and opsonization must not be treated as one universal geometric failure.
Primary filtering studies were available as indexed article text/abstract, but full-text opens encountered access challenges; preserved numerical dimensions still require later full-text recheck.

functional_sequences.mechanism: Blood-borne material reaches the open circulation; white-pulp T-cell and follicular B-cell compartments support adaptive responses.

steps.caption: Blood-borne antigen is exposed to open red-pulp and follicular-surface compartments.
steps.cue: Gold antigen icons are separate from red-cell symbols; local access is shown without prescribing a unique human trafficking route.

steps.caption: The PALS is a T-cell compartment associated with central arteries.
steps.cue: Use compartment highlighting; antigen presentation is an explanatory inset, not proof of an individual dendritic-cell track.

steps.caption: Follicular B cells recognize antigen; human superficial follicular zones differ from rodent marginal zones.
steps.cue: T- and B-compartment identities are functional; avoid depicting a rodent marginal sinus or importing mouse bridging channels.

steps.caption: A responding B cell can receive cognate T-cell help.
steps.cue: Schematic interaction card at the T/B interface; no validated human cell migration trajectory is claimed.

steps.caption: A responding secondary follicle supports proliferation and selection of B cells.
steps.cue: Human splenic T-follicular-helper cells are documented in germinal centres; helper signals are diagrammatic, not mesh parts.

steps.caption: The adaptive response can produce antibody-secreting cells and memory B cells.
steps.cue: Antibody output uses an explanatory card; no fixed efferent lymphatic route or fixed memory-cell address is animated.

schematic_limitations: The source models responding germinal centres; this is one activation state, not a claim that every adult follicle is activated.
Exact human antigen-transfer and lymphocyte ingress/egress trajectories remain insufficiently resolved; display them as explanatory cards.
Human splenic T-follicular-helper localization/signals are supported by control and ITP specimens; this timeline does not model ITP.
No stage duration denotes real immune-response time; GC activation is not blood-flow motion.
Memory B-cell location is not confined to the superficial zone; human phenotypic distributions and nomenclature are complex.
